la:noun:mel.html:
mĕl, mellis (
abl. sing. melli, .—Gen. and dat. plur. obsol. acc. to P.), n.
Gr. μέλι, honey; μέλισσα, bee; cf. mulsus
, honey.
Lit.: hoc est melli dulci dulcius, (Spengel, dulce): villa abundat lacte, caseo, melle,; cf. : roscida mella,: mellis vindemia,.—
Trop., honey for sweetness, pleasantness: poëtica mella,: hoc juvat et melli est,is pleasant,.—Of sweetness, pleasantness of speech: Nestoreum mel, Auct. Pan. ad Pison. 64: Homerici senis mella,.— Prov.: quia te tango, mel mihi videor lingere,it seems to me as sweet as honey,: mella petere in medio flumine,of a vain search,. —As a term of endearment, darling, sweet, honey: meum mel, meum cor,; ; ; : Sempronium, mel ac delicias tuas, Cael. ap. .
